S070-01.notes: Colon gloss 'stars were thought to remain exactly as they had always been' defines immutable. A (unfathomable) and D (imperceptible) clash with stars being visible/studied; B (inhospitable) is off-topic. Tycho's Nov 1572 nova in Cassiopeia and his parallax argument placing it beyond the Moon are accurate.

S070-02.notes: Harvest/replant creates young stands that fires once produced. B not supported (replanting does not eliminate fire); C and D contradict the young-stand requirement. 167 singing males in 1974 and 5-20-year jack pine stands are accurate.

S070-03.notes: 48-41=7; 41-33=8; 8>7 supports the claim. D is the only choice giving both drops. A (15) is the total; C gives only one drop; B irrelevant. Numbers in D compute correctly.

S070-04.notes: B states the purpose (live deliberately, essential facts, learn what it had to teach). All four quotations match Walden's text verbatim (Visitors; Where I Lived; Where I Lived; Economy). C concerns simplicity but not the experiment's purpose. Dates 1845-1847 and 1854 publication accurate.

S070-05.notes: A reverses the result; B overstates detail; D wrong (Wu did not win). Facts accurate: Lee-Yang 1956 proposal, Wu's Co-60 experiment at ~mK temperatures (run late 1956, published early 1957; 'later that year ... found' is acceptable since decisive data came Dec 1956), 1957 Nobel to Lee and Yang only.

flags.note: 'Each of the system's symbols stands for a syllable' is a slight overgeneralization: one character of the Cherokee syllabary (s) represents a lone consonant. Consider 'Nearly every symbol' or 'Each symbol ... stands for a sound, usually a syllable' if strict accuracy is desired; common simplification otherwise.

S070-06.notes: Subject 'Each' is singular -> 'stands for'; present tense matches 'stands for' generic description. B/C/D are plural. Sequoyah (silversmith) completed the syllabary 1821: accurate.

S070-07.notes: Colon introduces the two named skyscrapers after an independent clause. A semicolon needs an independent clause after it; B runs together; C 'being' is ungrammatical/wordy. Facts: Khan's framed tube (1960s), trussed tube at Hancock, bundled tube at Sears/Willis — 'versions of it' accurate.

S070-08.notes: Hair-cutting is a specific instance of pressure to abandon customs. A implies contrast; C implies a parallel separate point; D implies replacement. Facts accurate: Yankton Dakota, Atlantic Monthly Jan-Mar 1900, 'short hair was worn by mourners, and shingled hair by cowards.'

S070-09.notes: Only D contrasts the properties of gelatin and agar. 'resists most bacteria' is a fair paraphrase of 'few bacteria can break it down'. Hesse/agar history (1881, Koch's lab context) accurate.

S070-10.notes: Inverted sentence; true subject is 'the Babylonian Map of the World' (singular) -> 'is'. 'attempts' is in the prepositional phrase (trap for A/B). D creates a fragment. Tablet dated c. 6th century BCE showing Babylon ringed by a circular ocean: accurate.
